recognize_zh: 這顆顆粒球比一般嗜中性球大，細胞核分成約 8–10 個以上擠在一起的葉（hypersegmentation），細胞質有細小中性顆粒；巨大且過度分葉的嗜中性球屬於顆粒球異常形態，常見於巨母紅血球性貧血、G-CSF 或藥物影響。
features: Enlarged neutrophil (macropolycyte), roughly 1.5-2 times the diameter of adjacent red cells
Markedly hypersegmented nucleus with numerous (well over 6) clustered lobes
Coarse, clumped mature chromatin in each lobe
Cytoplasm with fine neutrophilic granulation, no toxic granulation or Dohle bodies evident
Background red cells show mild anisocytosis without obvious schistocytes
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows an enlarged neutrophil with a markedly hypersegmented nucleus composed of numerous clustered lobes of mature, clumped chromatin, and cytoplasm with fine neutrophilic granules. Adjacent red cells show mild anisocytosis. Giant hypersegmented neutrophils (macropolycytes) are a dysplastic-appearing granulocyte change that is most often reactive or nutritional, as seen with vitamin B12/folate deficiency, antimetabolite therapy (e.g., methotrexate, hydroxyurea) or growth factor exposure. Findings are consistent with a dysplastic (hypersegmented, giant) granulocyte; clinical correlation, B12/folate levels and medication history are recommended before attributing it to a myelodysplastic neoplasm.

ddx.vs: Megaloblastic anemia shows the same hypersegmented neutrophils together with macro-ovalocytes and low B12/folate; the neutrophil alone cannot separate it from drug effect.
MDS more typically shows hypogranular or pseudo-Pelger-Huet hyposegmented neutrophils with cytopenias and clonal cytogenetic abnormalities, rather than isolated hypersegmentation.
The hereditary form affects most neutrophils in an otherwise healthy person without macrocytosis, whereas acquired forms occur with nutritional deficiency or drugs.
